reader: The charter's capable eight-year-old learner, studying the physics lesson independently in Chinese or English.
jobStory: When I meet a semiconductor sensor, I want to understand what makes its current change, so I can distinguish a temperature response from a light response and follow the printed worked calculations.
evidence: Charter product.md, card113 faithful prose and the human's bounded TEXT AUTHOR instructions. Reader phrasing is an author assumption, not user research.
question: How can a semiconductor turn temperature or light into a change in electrical current?
priority: Resistance depends on temperature; distinguish the thermistor component from the complete measuring instrument.
Absorbed radiation heats a bolometer; keep the old distant-match sensitivity claim conditional and historical.
Illumination can increase conductivity even at constant temperature; explain the two source circuits without inventing calibration.
Light supplies energy to free charge carriers; explain electrons and holes without treating a hole as a physical cavity.
Name the photoresistor and its source-described small size and sensitivity without a universal device promise.
Retain both numbered printed examples as complete worked examples, with givens, reasoning, equations and registered corrected results.

contentModel.prose: Exactly the source's thirteen ordered objects, same kind, stable source_refs, figure identity and complete source_text snapshot. Rewrite only the learner-facing text; figures remain unedited.
contentModel.examples: Exactly two source objects, original numbers/groups/pages/figure_refs, full printed solutions. No choices, answer keys, keyboard interaction or added tasks.
contentModel.translation: One English counterpart for every normalized Chinese lesson object and each worked example; exact matching formula tokens and preserved source snapshots.
contentModel.missingEvidence: Do not invent device specifications or conditions for the historical match claim. Independent science and modern-figure acceptance remain dependencies.

cut: New practice questions and all t18 authoring.
A universal claim that any bolometer can detect a match several kilometres away.
The literal solution's false implication that an electrolyte inside the sphere has no ions; retain the intended small-hole, negligible inner-field approximation.
Advanced band diagrams, unsourced modern sensitivity numbers, artificial summary and FAQ.
copyCheck: Evidence, item-specific relevance and deletion tests applied to each explanation; source-method and approval notes stay outside learner text.
